topic: Why modern electric vehicle batteries are still expensive
angle: The Cathode Choke: Why plummeting battery cell pack dreams collided with the harsh reality of raw mineral refining bottlenecks and thermal management overhead.
summary: While lithium-ion pack costs plummeted by over 80% between 2010 and 2020, price declines have hit a hard thermodynamic and geopolitical floor between $115 and $140 per kilowatt-hour. Over 70% of a modern battery cell's cost is now dictated strictly by raw precursor chemicals—specifically battery-grade lithium hydroxide, Class-1 nickel, and synthetic graphite. With more than 75% of global cathode precursor refining concentrated in a single geographic corridor, Western automakers face compounding regulatory tariffs and multi-billion-dollar supply contracts that prevent electric vehicles from reaching true sticker price parity with legacy combustion platforms.

facts.statement: Raw mineral and chemical precursor costs represent between 68% and 77% of the total manufacturing cost of an automotive-grade NCM811 battery cell.
